questions.q: What does Eyal say is the real source of distraction?
a: Internal triggers such as anxiety or boredom
Notifications from phones and computers
A lack of discipline and willpower
Friends and coworkers interrupting you
questions.why: Lesson 1 says gadgets are not the root cause; the triggers wired inside us make us seek distraction.

questions.q: What does the summary suggest doing when you feel the urge to get distracted?
a: Notice the emotion behind it and let it pass
Remove every device from the room
Switch to a different task for a while
Promise yourself a reward afterwards
questions.why: Lesson 1 advises identifying the feeling and visualizing it being carried away like water or wind.

a: You reserve fixed slots for specific tasks each week
You work until a task is finished, then rest
You track how long every task actually took
You set a timer and stop whenever it rings
questions.why: Lesson 2 defines it as allocating a set time frame to a task, then protecting that time from distraction.

questions.q: What does Eyal say belongs on your calendar alongside work?
a: Quality time for yourself, family and friends
The most urgent work deadline
Exercise and meal preparation
Email and administrative tasks
questions.why: Lesson 2 says to start by planning quality time for yourself and the people close to you.

a: Defining yourself as someone with the habits you want
Fining yourself each time you break a promise
Studying alongside a stranger online
Telling friends about a goal so they hold you to it
questions.why: Lesson 3 suggests saying you are a vegetarian rather than that you cannot eat meat, to avoid temptation.
